display.purpose: Landing headline and the verdict word.

headline.purpose: Section titles, page headers, footer call, verdict word on small screens.

title.purpose: Check-row labels, panel and receipt titles, timeline employers.

lead.purpose: The single paragraph under a display or headline.

label.purpose: Field labels, legend entries, receipt keys; uppercase tracked only for status words.

wordmark.purpose: CONSTANCIA beside the closed 24px seal, top-left of every nav.

mono.purpose: Hashes, keys, DIDs and measured values only.

motion.name: ease-resolve
motion.purpose: Exponential ease-out, no bounce, for seal segments and the verdict wipe.

motion.name: seal-segment
motion.purpose: Segment fill/border change; landing close uses 120ms stagger.

motion.name: seal-blink
motion.purpose: CHECKING segment and chip: two hard steps, no shimmer.

motion.name: verdict-wipe
motion.value: clip-path inset(0 100% 0 0) to inset(0) over 600ms ease-resolve
motion.purpose: Verdict colour wipes in once from the seal side.

motion.name: control-hover
motion.purpose: Button, copy and drop-slot colour inversions.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Seal and verdict change instantly; nothing blinks.

components.name: Primary Button

components.name: Secondary Button

narrative.overview:
Constancia is drawn as an institution with an identity manual, in the lineage of Venezuelan modernist identity programs of the 1960s and 70s: banks, museums, the Caracas Metro. The whole system rests on one geometric mark, a C built from five segments on a 6x6 module grid, and that mark is not decoration: it is the verifier. Each segment is one check, in fixed order (Constancia, Acreditado, Firma, Titular, Registro), and it changes state in place. It never moves, never reorders.

The palette is two values plus one colour. Pure white paper and near-black ink carry everything; an institutional marigold owns whole regions (the seal column, the closing footer band, the "no se puede verificar ahora" verdict) and is never used for small text. Green and red exist only to report a verdict. Structure comes from black rules at 2, 3 and 4px, a strict 12-column grid and square corners everywhere. There are no shadows, no gradients and no rounded corners; the Tailwind theme resets `--radius-*`, `--shadow-*` and the default colour palette so they cannot be reached for.

Density is calm and projector-safe: body text never below 17px, targets at least 48px, one focal piece per screen. Operate surfaces (`/verify`, `/vault`, `/cv`, `/employer`, `/ledger`) inherit the same world with more restraint: the marigold seal column appears where a check result is the subject, and white with black rules elsewhere.
keyCharacteristics: One mark, five segments, one check per segment; state changes in place.
White, black, one marigold; verdict green and red only on states.
Square corners, black rules of 2 / 3 / 4px, no shadows, no gradients.
Heavy neo-grotesk display, mono only for hashes and IDs.
State is never colour alone: every state carries a word and a drawn mark.

rules.name: The Two Values and One Colour Rule
rules.body: Paper, ink and marigold are the world. Green and red appear only where a result is being reported; there are no decorative greys, tints or extra accents, and the theme does not expose any.

rules.name: The Marigold Region Rule
rules.body: Marigold owns areas, not details: a column, a band, a verdict field, a status notice, a state chip. It never colours text, rules or icons, and text set on it is always ink.

rules.name: The Status Word Rule
rules.body: Uppercase, bold, tracked small text is reserved for a state word printed next to its chip or segment (VERIFICADO, FALLÓ, NO DISPONIBLE). It never sits above a heading as a label.

rules.name: The Mono Is Data Rule
rules.body: Red Hat Mono appears only on machine values. Headings, buttons and prose never use it.

rules.name: The Fixed Position Rule
rules.body: Rows, segments and checks keep their position through every state. Results replace in place; nothing reorders or slides to announce a change.

rules.name: The Rule Weight Rule
rules.body: Depth is drawn, not cast: a heavier black rule means a more important boundary. A section starts with a 4px top rule; rows inside it divide with 2px.

dos: Do keep every surface on paper, ink and marigold; use ok and fail only on verdicts, chips and status words.
Do give marigold whole regions (the 5/12 seal column, a band, a verdict field) and set only ink on it.
Do frame and divide with black rules: 4px for frames and section breaks, 3px for controls, 2px for rows.
Do print every state as a word plus a drawn mark, and keep it in its fixed position.
Do use the resolve ease (cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)) for the seal and the verdict wipe, and make both instant under reduced motion.
Do keep body text at 17px or more and every target at 48px or more.
Do set hashes, keys and IDs in Red Hat Mono with tabular numerals, shortened in the middle when long.
donts: Don't use rounded corners, shadows or gradients; the theme deliberately does not provide them.
Don't set marigold as text, rule or icon colour, or put white text on marigold.
Don't introduce greys beyond ink-muted (secondary text) and rule (hairlines), or use either as a fill.
Don't place an uppercase label or kicker above a heading; uppercase tracking is for status words only.
Don't reorder, slide or reflow checks to show progress; segments and rows change state in place.
Don't show a state through colour alone, or a disabled control through opacity alone on buttons.
Don't use glyph or icon-font icons; marks are drawn square-capped SVG strokes.
